issues.description: The template's make_y_state function signature is missing the depolarization probability parameter 'p' that the problem statement requires and that the solution implements. The problem statement specifies make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None and other parts of the exercise (and the solution) call or implement make_y_state with a 'p' parameter. The template definition def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int) -> None therefore prevents students from implementing or testing the intended noisy preparation behavior and will cause signature mismatches when integrating with other provided functions.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to include the depolarization parameter 'p', matching the problem statement and solution: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Also update the template docstring to match the signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution define make_y_state(circ, q, p) with a depolarization probability parameter p, but the template's make_y_state stub is declared as make_y_state(circ, q) (missing the p parameter). This mismatch will confuse students and cause failures when following the spec or running tests that call make_y_state with three arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template stub to match the problem and solution signatures: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None: and update its docstring/body accordingly so students can pass the depolarization parameter p as specified in the exercise.
